exposure: Mode of delivery (Cesarean delivery vs Vaginal delivery)
cohort: 102 women with perianal Crohn's disease who have given birth, selected from the 1000 inflammatory bowel disease cohort of a tertiary hospital in the Netherlands
finding: No significant relationship was found between mode of delivery (Cesarean vs Vaginal) and fecal incontinence or perianal disease progression in women with perianal Crohn's disease.
mod_finding: Fecal incontinence and perianal disease progression after vaginal delivery in Crohn's disease women with active perianal fistula is not significantly increased in this retrospective cohort.
